newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac, Juppe ratings soar on immigration debate.
newsitem.headline: Chirac, Juppe ratings soar on immigration debate.

text.p: The popularity of French President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe has soared following their drive for a controversial bill to clamp down on illegal immigrants, a poll showed on Thursday.
The Sofres survey for Figaro Magazine showed that 41 percent of those questioned trusted Chirac to solve France's problems, up from 35 percent in a similar poll last month.
Juppe's score rose to 35 percent from 30 percent over the same period.
The bill, being debated in the National Assembly, aims to close loopholes in an already tough 1993 law and would grant police extended powers to track immigrants in France.

Artists, intellectuals and film-makers have spearheaded opposition to the legislation, accusing the centre-right government of pandering to growing numbers of extreme-right National Front voters ahead of general elections in 1998.

Some 100,000 people marched through Paris last Saturday in a peaceful protest against the legislation, which some critics have likened to anti-Jewish laws of the Vichy regime that ruled France during the Nazi occupation.
A second protest in Paris on Tuesday night turned violent when demonstrators threw rocks at police. Forty protesters were detained and 30 riot policement hurt in the melee.
